name: China
description: One of humanity's oldest continuous civilizations, originating paper, printing, gunpowder, silk, philosophical Confucianism/Daoism, the Great Wall, and imperial dynasties.

kingdoms.title: Han Dynasty (The Golden Age of China)
kingdoms.description: The imperial golden age that defined Chinese cultural identity, institutionalized Confucian statecraft, and opened the ancient Silk Road across Eurasia.

kingdoms.title: Ming Dynasty (The Great Ming)
kingdoms.description: Native Chinese imperial restoration renowned for constructing the Forbidden City, expanding the Great Wall in stone brick, and sponsoring Zheng He's maritime treasure fleets.

kingdoms.title: Qin Dynasty (First Imperial Unification)
kingdoms.description: The revolutionary dynasty that first unified China under Qin Shi Huang, standardizing currency, writing, weights, and creating the Terracotta Army and early Great Wall.

kingdoms.title: Song Dynasty (The Renaissance of Science & Arts)
kingdoms.description: Era of extraordinary technological innovation, inventing gunpowder, the magnetic compass, paper money, and movable type printing alongside Neo-Confucian philosophy.

kingdoms.title: Tang Dynasty (The Cosmopolitan Empire)
kingdoms.description: Regarded as the high point of Chinese civilization, characterized by unsurpassed poetry, international Silk Road trade, Buddhist arts, and global cosmopolitanism.

kings.title: Emperor Taizong of Tang (Li Shimin)
kings.biography: Co-founder and golden ruler of the Tang Dynasty, revered as 'Heavenly Khagan' by nomadic tribes for his military brilliance, religious tolerance, meritocratic civil service exams, and economic prosperity.
kings.internationalConnections: Welcomed Nestorian Christians, Zoroastrians, and Indian Buddhist monk Xuanzang to the imperial court in Chang'an.

kings.title: Emperor Wu of Han (Liu Che)
kings.kingdom: Han Dynasty (The Golden Age of China)
kings.biography: Regarded as one of China's greatest emperors; he established state Confucianism, doubled the empire's territory, and dispatched explorer Zhang Qian westward, inaugurating the ancient Silk Road.
kings.internationalConnections: Opened direct trade corridors with the Greco-Bactrian kingdoms, Fergana (Heavenly Horses), and Parthia.

kings.title: Empress Wu Zetian (Shengshen Huangdi)
kings.biography: The only female emperor regnant in 4,000 years of Chinese history. Founded the Second Zhou Dynasty, elevated merit-based scholar-officials, fostered Buddhism, and patronized the Longmen Grottoes.
kings.internationalConnections: Secured Tang protectorates along the Tarim Basin and maintained Silk Road diplomatic stability.

kings.title: Qin Shi Huang (First Sovereign Emperor)
kings.biography: First Emperor of unified China who abolished feudalism, centralized administration, standardized Chinese characters, currency, axle widths, and constructed the Terracotta Army and the Great Wall.
kings.internationalConnections: Connected northern defensive fortifications against the Xiongnu nomadic confederation.

kings.title: Yongle Emperor (Zhu Di)
kings.biography: Visionary Ming emperor who moved the capital to Beijing, constructed the Forbidden City, rebuilt the Grand Canal, compiled the Yongle Encyclopedia, and sponsored Admiral Zheng He's seven epic maritime treasure voyages.
kings.internationalConnections: Zheng He's treasure fleet established diplomatic ties with Sri Lanka (Kotte), India (Calicut), Hormuz, and East Africa (Malindi).

sites.name: Mogao Caves (Caves of the Thousand Buddhas)
sites.description: Network of 492 cave sanctuaries carved into a cliff at the Silk Road junction of Dunhuang, housing 45,000 square meters of Buddhist murals.
sites.history: Served as a spiritual nexus for merchants, pilgrims, and scholars traveling the Silk Road across the Gobi Desert.
sites.construction: Carved into sandstone conglomerate cliffs, decorated with mineral pigments including lapis lazuli, malachite, and gold leaf.
sites.architecture: Contains colossal seated Buddha statues up to 35 meters tall and the secret Library Cave (Cave 17) holding ancient manuscripts in multiple languages.
sites.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the world's richest repository of Silk Road art.
sites.currentStatus: Protected in Dunhuang, Gansu Province, China.

sites.name: Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang
sites.description: Subterranean army of 8,000 unique life-sized soldiers, acclaimed as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.
sites.history: Constructed to guard the first Emperor of unified China, Qin Shi Huang, in the afterlife. Discovered by local farmers in Lintong District, Xi'an in 1974.
sites.construction: Over 700,000 workers molded and fired individual terracotta figures, each with distinct facial features, hairstyles, armor, and bronze weaponry.
sites.architecture: Massive four-pit subterranean necropolis covering over 56 square kilometers, originally painted in vibrant cinnabar, malachite, and azurite pigments.
sites.significance: Acclaimed worldwide as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' following French Prime Minister Jacques Chirac's declaration in 1978; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
sites.currentStatus: Excavated and displayed in the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum.
sites.wonderCategory: Eighth Wonder of the World (International Acclaim)
sites.wonderHistoricalContext: In 1978, during an official state visit, French statesman Jacques Chirac declared: 'There were Seven Wonders in the world, and the discovery of the Terracotta Army is the Eighth.' It remains universally recognized under this title.

sites.name: The Forbidden City (Imperial Palace)
sites.description: The world's largest palatial complex, spanning 720,000 square meters with 980 surviving buildings and 8,886 bays of rooms.
sites.history: Served as the home of 24 Chinese emperors across the Ming and Qing Dynasties from 1420 to 1924 CE.
sites.construction: Built by over one million workers using precision interlocking timber bracket joinery (Dougong) without a single iron nail.
sites.architecture: Strict North-South axial Feng Shui alignment, yellow glazed imperial roof tiles, white marble terraces, and deep crimson walls.
sites.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the supreme monument of traditional Chinese architecture.
sites.currentStatus: Standing pristine as the Palace Museum in the heart of Beijing.

sites.name: The Great Wall of China
sites.description: Massive 21,196 km military defensive fortification network, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
sites.history: Built and continuously expanded across successive Chinese dynasties to protect against nomadic raids and secure Silk Road trade. The most prominent surviving stone brick sections were built during the Ming Dynasty.
sites.construction: Constructed from tamped earth, granite, limestone, and kiln-fired bricks held together by sticky rice mortar.
sites.architecture: Features defensive watchtowers, beacon signaling towers, garrison fortresses, and tactical crenellations across mountainous terrain.
sites.significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
sites.currentStatus: Standing and preserved across multiple provinces in northern China.
sites.wonderHistoricalContext: Chosen by over 100 million global voters in Lisbon on July 7, 2007 (07/07/07) as a premier New 7 Wonder of the World, representing humanity's greatest defensive engineering achievement.
